text: The number of s-electrons present in an ion with 55 protons in its unipositive state is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The number of protons in an element determines its atomic number, which is the number of electrons in a neutral atom of the element. The unipositive state of an ion indicates that it has lost one electron. Therefore, the number of electrons in a unipositive ion is one less than the atomic number.

The element with 55 protons is cesium (Cs), which is in group 1 of the periodic table. Group 1 elements have one valence electron in the s sublevel of their outermost energy level.

In a neutral atom of cesium, there are 55 electrons, with the electron configuration [Xe] $6s^{1}$. When cesium loses one electron to form a unipositive ion $(Cs^{+})$, the resulting ion has 54 electrons.

Out of this 54 electrons s subshell has 10 electrons in $1s^{2}, 2s^{2}, 3s^{2}, 4s^{2}, 5s^{2}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text: What is the number of unpaired electron(s) in the highest occupied molecular orbital of the following species : $\mathrm{N}_{2};\mathrm{N}_{2}^{+};\mathrm{O}_{2};\mathrm{O}_{2}^{+}$ ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For molecules up to $\mathrm{N}{}_{2}$ the $σ2p_{z}$ orbital lies above $π2p_{x}$, $π2p_{y}$; from $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$ onwards it lies below them.

$\mathrm{N}{}_{2}$ (14 electrons): $σ1s^{2}\qquad σ^{\ast }1s^{2}σ2s^{2}σ^{\ast }2s^{2}π2p_{x}^{2}=π2p_{y}^{2}σ2p_{z}^{2}$. The HOMO $σ2p_{z}$ holds a pair, so it has 0 unpaired electrons.

$\mathrm{N}{}_{2}{}^{+}$ (13 electrons): the HOMO is $σ2p_{z}^{1}$, so 1 unpaired electron.

$\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$ (16 electrons): $σ1s^{2}\qquad σ^{\ast }1s^{2}σ2s^{2}σ^{\ast }2s^{2}σ2p_{z}^{2}π2p_{x}^{2}=π2p_{y}^{2}π^{\ast }2p_{x}^{1}=π^{\ast }2p_{y}^{1}$. The HOMO is the degenerate $π^{\ast }2p$ pair with one electron in each, so 2 unpaired electrons.

$\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{+}$ (15 electrons): the HOMO is $π^{\ast }2p_{x}^{1}$, so 1 unpaired electron.

The numbers are 0, 1, 2, 1.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion A : Benzene is more stable than hypothetical cyclohexatriene

Reason R : The delocalised $π$ electron cloud is attracted more strongly by nuclei of carbon atoms.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT  the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Benzene is more stable than hypothetical cyclohexatriene due to the delocalization of electrons in the π electron cloud of the aromatic ring. This delocalization of electrons leads to a more stable electronic configuration in benzene, as the electrons are shared more evenly between all six carbon atoms in the ring. This is in agreement with Assertion A.

Reason R is also correct, as the delocalized π electron cloud in the aromatic ring is attracted more strongly by the nuclei of the carbon atoms. This is due to the fact that the π electrons in the ring are more spread out and are not localized to a single atom, which makes them more attracted to the positively charged nuclei of the carbon atoms. This explanation supports Assertion A.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text:
A student has studied the decomposition of a gas AB${}_{3}$ at 25${}^{\circ }$C. He obtained the following data.

  
    p (mm Hg)
    50
    100
    200
    400
  

  
    relative t${}_{1/2}$ (s)
    4
    2
    1
    0.5
  

The order of the reaction is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a reaction of order $n$, the half-life depends on the initial pressure as

$t_{1/2}\propto p_{0}^{1-n}$

From the data, each doubling of $p_{0}$ (50 to 100 mm Hg) halves $t_{1/2}$ (4 s to 2 s):

$\dfrac{4}{2}=\left (\dfrac{50}{100}\right )^{1-n}\Rightarrow 2=2^{n-1}\Rightarrow n-1=1\Rightarrow n=2$

The other pairs (200 to 400 mm Hg, 1 s to 0.5 s) give the same ratio, so $t_{1/2}\propto \dfrac{1}{p_{0}}$, which is characteristic of a second order reaction.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text: Total number of tripeptides possible by mixing of valine and proline is $___________$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To calculate the total number of tripeptides possible by mixing valine and proline, we need to use the fundamental principle of counting.

Since a tripeptide is made up of three amino acids, and we have two choices for each position (either valine or proline), we can use the multiplication principle to find the total number of possible tripeptides.

That is, the total number of tripeptides possible by mixing valine and proline is:

2 x 2 x 2 = 8

Therefore, there are a total of 8 possible tripeptides that can be formed by mixing valine and proline.

text:
One mole of an ideal monoatomic gas is subjected to changes as shown in the graph. The magnitude of the work done (by the system or on the system) is $__________ J ($nearest integer)


[IMG]


Given ; $\log 2=0.3$

$\ln 10=2.3$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From the graph: state 1 is ($1.0$ bar, $20$ L), state 2 is ($1.0$ bar, $40$ L) and state 3 is ($0.5$ bar, $40$ L). At states 1 and 3, $PV=20$ bar L, so $3\to 1$ is an isotherm with $nRT=20$ bar L.

$1\to 2$ (isobaric expansion): $w=-P\Delta V=-1.0\times (40-20)=-20$ bar L.

$2\to 3$ (isochoric): $w=0$.

$3\to 1$ (isothermal compression from $V_{i}=40$ L to $V_{f}=20$ L):

$w=-nRT\ln \dfrac{V_{f}}{V_{i}}=-20\ln \dfrac{20}{40}=20\ln 2=20\times 2.3\times 0.3=13.8\text{bar L}$

Net work: $w=-20+0+13.8=-6.2$ bar L.

Since $1\text{bar}=10^{5}$ Pa and $1\text{L}=10^{-3}\text{m}^{3}$, $1$ bar L $=100$ J, so $|w|=6.2\times 100=620$ J.

Hence, the answer is 620.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text: Maximum number of isomeric monochloro derivatives which can be obtained from 2,2,5,5-tetramethylhexane by chlorination is $_____________$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
2,2,5,5-Tetramethylhexane is $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}$; it has only two kinds of hydrogen: 18 equivalent methyl H and 4 equivalent $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ H.

Replacing a methyl H gives $\mathrm{ClCH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}$ (1-chloro-2,2,5,5-tetramethylhexane), which has no stereocentre: 1 isomer.

Replacing a $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ H gives $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CHCl}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}$ (3-chloro-2,2,5,5-tetramethylhexane). C3 carries four different groups ($\mathrm{H}$, $\mathrm{Cl}$, $\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}$, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}$), so it is chiral and exists as a pair of enantiomers: 2 isomers.

Maximum number of monochloro isomers $=1+2=3$.

Hence, the answer is 3.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text:
The total pressure observed by mixing two liquids A and B is 350 mm Hg when their mole fractions are 0.7 and 0.3 respectively.

The total pressure becomes 410 mm Hg if the mole fractions are changed to 0.2 and 0.8 respectively for A and B. The vapour pressure of pure A is $__________ mm Hg. ($Nearest integer)

Consider the liquids and solutions behave ideally.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $V.P$ of pure $A$ be $P_{A}^{0}$

Let $V.P$ of pure $B$ be $P_{B}^{0}$

When $\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{A}}=0.7&\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{B}}=0.3$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{s}}=350 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}^{0}\times 0.7+\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}^{0}\times 0.3=350 \end{array}$

When $\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{A}}=0.2&\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{B}}=0.8$

$\begin{array}{l} P_{\mathrm{s}}=410 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}^{0}\times 0.2+\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}^{0}\times 0.8=410 \end{array}$

Solving (i) and (ii)

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}^{0}=314\mathrm{mm}\mathrm{Hg} \\  \\ \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}^{0}=434\mathrm{mm}\mathrm{Hg} \\  \\ \therefore \text{Answer}=314 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text:
If the pKa of lactic acid is 5, then the pH of 0.005 M calcium lactate solution at 25${}^{\circ }$C is $___________$ $\times$ 10${}^{-1}$ (Nearest integer)


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Concentration of calcium lactate $=0.005\mathrm{M}$, concentration of lactate ion $=(2\times 0.005)\mathrm{M}$. 

Calcium lactate is a salt of weak acid $+$ strong base

 $\therefore$ Salt hydrolysis will take place.

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{pH}=7+\dfrac{1}{2}(\mathrm{pKa}+\log \mathrm{C}) \\  \\ =7+\dfrac{1}{2}(5+\log (2\times 0.005)) \\  \\ =7+\dfrac{1}{2}[5-2\log 10]=7+\dfrac{1}{2}\times 3=8.5=85\times 10^{-1} \end{array}$
